statements.context: Questioning during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on AI and information technology in the Department of Defense.

statements.text: The second piece is we have taken a very, very hard look at artificial intelligence and machine learning to look at, you know, the defense of the DOD Information Network. [...] AI and ML [machine learning] is doing that in some part today.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on cyberspace operations, featuring testimony from General Nakasone, Commander of U.S. Cyber Command.

statements.text: I'm curious—and I guess we could do it in the context of AUKUS Pillar II, but we could do it more broadly—I'm just concerned on an ongoing basis, as we are developing technology, advanced technology, and defenses together, the issue of artificial intelligence, and AI is a concern, a growing concern about making sure we have controls over that kind of advanced technology. So, it cannot get out of control or be misused somehow.
statements.context: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing on modernizing U.S. arms exports and strengthening AUKUS.

statements.text: Could you give this committee, as a follow-up, some suggestions on procurement changes just within the area of AI?
statements.context: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing titled 'Man and Machine: Artificial Intelligence on the Battlefield,' where a member solicits reform proposals for DoD AI procurement.

statements.text: Is there an area where, because of our privacy protections— which is something we shouldn't change in our country—where we might be at an inherent disadvantage with China?
statements.venue: House Armed Services Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation hearing 'Man and Machine: Artificial Intelligence on the Battlefield'

statements.text: And with AI they can take biochemicals at very limited cost with only a handful of people doing it and kill millions of people.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on advanced research and technology threats.

statements.text: I think with the race that is going on between the development of artificial intelligence and then our ability to deal with that artificial intelligence, how to react to that on our own — [...] but also on a general sense our enemies, some of the countries I just mentioned, are they in a situation where you see them developing that kind of capability, too, to counter that as well, to keep up with it on the responding side of it?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing reviewing the Defense Intelligence Enterprise's posture and capabilities in strategic competition with China.

statements.text: The key battle for the prosperity of the next generation will be whether China or the US, with our partners, sets the standards for AI, biomedicine, and energy technologies. These aren’t things that even the world’s largest economy can compel. They will be agreed among trading partners.
statements.context: Statement submitted for the House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing on State Department restructuring and arms control.
